newsitem.title: USA: IRS meets with muni groups on yield burning.
newsitem.headline: IRS meets with muni groups on yield burning.

text.p: Officials of the U.S. Treasury Department and the Internal Revenue Service met with municipal bond groups on Thursday to discuss the federal government's controversial ruling on yield burning.

Federal officials assured the bond groups that their concerns would be "thoroughly reviewed and that a response to the issues raised would be soon in coming," the National League of Cities said in a statement.

The ruling stemmed from allegations that underwriters in the municipal bond market overcharged issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond refundings, a practice dubbed yield burning.
The IRS on July 19 said issuers of advance refunding bonds can enter into "closing agreements" with the IRS to head off possibly having the interest on their bonds declared taxable.

Municipalities would have to agree to pay the Treasury the difference between the price they paid and the spot price of the securities on the purchase date, plus interest on that figures under the IRS revenue procedure.
The NLC, the Government Finance Officers Association and other organizations involved with state and local governments have appealed to the Treasury Department to rethink the matter.
The NLC said the IRS ruling constitutes "a harsh, retroactive, unfunded federal mandate on cities," and urged the IRS to go after the underwriters who overcharged cities.
